verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, according to the command of God our Savior and of the Lord Jesus Christ, our hope,
verses.1:2: To Timothy, a genuine child in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and from Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.1:3: As I exhorted you to remain in Ephesus when I was traveling to Macedonia, that you might charge some not to teach a different doctrine,
verses.1:4: nor to devote attention to myths and unending genealogies, which produce disputes rather than the stewardship of God that is in faith—
verses.1:5: Now the goal of this charge is love issuing from a pure heart, a good conscience, and an unfeigned faith,
verses.1:6: from which some, having swerved, have turned away into fruitless talk,
verses.1:7: desiring to be teachers of the law, comprehending neither what they say nor the things they so confidently assert.
verses.1:8: Now we know that the law is good, provided one uses it lawfully,
verses.1:9: understanding this, that the law is not laid down for a righteous person, but for the lawless and unruly, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for slayers of fathers and slayers of mothers, for murderers,
verses.1:10: for the sexually immoral, for men who lie with men, for enslavers, for liars, for perjurers, and for anything else that stands opposed to sound doctrine,
verses.1:11: in accordance with the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, with which I have been entrusted.
verses.1:12: I give thanks to Christ Jesus our Lord, who has strengthened me, because He judged me faithful, appointing me to ministry,
verses.1:13: though formerly I was a blasphemer, a persecutor, and an insolent oppressor; yet I received mercy, because I acted ignorantly in unbelief,
verses.1:14: and the grace of our Lord overflowed exceedingly, together with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
verses.1:15: Faithful is the saying and worthy of complete acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the foremost;
verses.1:16: yet for this very reason I received mercy, that in me as the foremost, Jesus Christ might display His utmost longsuffering, as an example for those who are to believe in Him for eternal life.
verses.1:17: Now to the King of the ages, incorruptible, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.1:18: This charge I entrust to you, child Timothy, according to the prophecies formerly spoken concerning you, that by them you may wage the noble warfare,
verses.1:19: holding faith and a good conscience, which some have thrust away and so have suffered shipwreck concerning the faith;
verses.1:20: among whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have handed over to Satan so that they may be disciplined not to blaspheme.
verses.2:1: First of all, then, I exhort that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be offered on behalf of all men,
verses.2:2: for kings and all who hold high station, that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and dignity.
verses.2:3: This is noble and acceptable before God our Savior,
verses.2:4: who wills that all men be saved and come to the full knowledge of the truth.
verses.2:5: For God is one, and one also is the Mediator between God and men, the Man Christ Jesus,
verses.2:6: who gave Himself as a ransom for all, the testimony borne at the proper times;
verses.2:7: for which I was appointed a herald and an apostle—I speak the truth in Christ, I do not lie—a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
verses.2:8: I desire, therefore, that in every place the men pray, lifting up holy hands without wrath or disputing;
verses.2:9: likewise also that women adorn themselves in respectable attire, with modesty and self-control, not with braided hair and gold, or pearls, or costly garments,
verses.2:10: but with what is fitting for women who profess godliness, through good works.
verses.2:11: Let a woman learn in quietness, in all submission.
verses.2:12: Now I do not allow a woman to teach, nor to hold authority over a man, but to be in quietness.
verses.2:13: For Adam was fashioned first, and afterward Eve;
verses.2:14: and Adam was not deceived, but the woman, having been thoroughly deceived, came into transgression.
verses.2:15: Yet she shall be saved through childbearing, if they abide in faith and love and sanctification, with self-control.
verses.3:1: Faithful is the saying: If anyone aspires to the office of an overseer, he sets his heart on a noble work.
verses.3:2: An overseer, therefore, must be irreproachable, the husband of one wife, temperate, prudent, orderly, hospitable, apt to teach,
verses.3:3: not addicted to wine, not violent, but forbearing, peaceable, free from the love of money,
verses.3:4: governing his own household well, keeping his children in submission with all dignity;
verses.3:5: (now if someone does not know how to govern his own household, how shall he care for the church of God?)
verses.3:6: not a recent convert, lest, being puffed up with conceit, he fall into the condemnation of the devil.
verses.3:7: Moreover, he must also have an honorable testimony from those outside, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.
verses.3:8: Deacons likewise must be dignified, not double-tongued, not indulging in much wine, not greedy for dishonest gain,
verses.3:9: holding fast the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
verses.3:10: And let these also be proved first; afterward let them serve as deacons, being blameless.
verses.3:11: Women likewise must be dignified, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.
verses.3:12: Let deacons be husbands of one wife, governing their children and their own households well.
verses.3:13: For those who have served well as deacons gain for themselves an honorable standing and great boldness in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:14: I am writing these things to you, hoping to come to you soon;
verses.3:15: yet if I am delayed, that you may know how one must conduct oneself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.
verses.3:16: And beyond dispute, great is the mystery of godliness: He who was manifested in the flesh, vindicated in the Spirit, seen by angels, heralded among the nations, believed on in the world, received up in glory.
verses.4:1: Now the Spirit explicitly declares that in later times some shall fall away from the faith, giving heed to deceiving spirits and teachings of demons,
verses.4:2: through the hypocrisy of those who speak lies, whose own conscience has been seared with a branding iron,
verses.4:3: forbidding marriage and commanding to abstain from foods which God created to be partaken of with thanksgiving by those who believe and have come to know the truth.
verses.4:4: For every created thing of God is good, and nothing is to be cast away when it is received with thanksgiving,
verses.4:5: for it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer.
verses.4:6: By setting these things before the brethren, you will be a good minister of Christ Jesus, nourished on the words of the faith and of the good teaching which you have closely followed.
verses.4:7: But refuse profane and old wives' tales; rather, train yourself for godliness.
verses.4:8: For bodily training is profitable for a little, yet godliness is profitable for all things, holding promise for the present life and for the life to come.
verses.4:9: Trustworthy is the saying and worthy of full acceptance.
verses.4:10: For to this end we labor and strive, because we have placed our hope in the living God, who is the Savior of all men, especially of those who believe.
verses.4:11: Command these things and teach them.
verses.4:12: Let no one look down upon your youth, but become a pattern for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
verses.4:13: Until I come, give close attention to the public reading, to exhortation, to teaching.
verses.4:14: Do not neglect the gift of grace that is in you, which was given to you through prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the eldership.
verses.4:15: Take pains with these things; be wholly given to them, so that your progress may be manifest to all.
verses.4:16: Pay close heed to yourself and to the teaching; persevere in these things, for in doing this you will save both yourself and those who hear you.
verses.5:1: Do not sharply rebuke an older man, but appeal to him as a father, younger men as brothers,
verses.5:2: older women as mothers, and younger women as sisters, in all purity.
verses.5:3: Give honor to widows who are widows indeed.
verses.5:4: But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to practice godliness toward their own household and to make repayment to their forebears, for this is acceptable in the sight of God.
verses.5:5: Now she who is a widow indeed, and left alone, has placed her hope in God and perseveres in supplications and prayers night and day;
verses.5:6: yet she who lives in self-indulgence is dead even while she lives.
verses.5:7: And charge them with these things, so that they may be above reproach.
verses.5:8: But if anyone fails to make provision for his own, and especially for members of his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
verses.5:9: Let a widow be enrolled only if she is no less than sixty years of age, having been the wife of one husband,
verses.5:10: well attested for noble deeds: if she has reared children, if she has shown hospitality to strangers, if she has washed the feet of the saints, if she has brought relief to the afflicted, and if she has diligently followed every good work.
verses.5:11: But refuse younger widows; for when their sensual desires turn them away from Christ, they wish to marry,
verses.5:12: thus incurring condemnation because they have cast aside their first pledge.
verses.5:13: And at the same time they also learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house; and not only idle, but gossips and busybodies as well, speaking things that ought not to be spoken.
verses.5:14: Therefore I desire that younger widows marry, bear children, manage the household, and give the adversary no occasion for reproach;
verses.5:15: for some have already strayed away after Satan.
verses.5:16: If any believing woman has widows, let her support them, and let the church not be burdened, so that it may support those who are widows indeed.
verses.5:17: Let the elders who govern well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in the word and in teaching.
verses.5:18: For the Scripture declares, "You shall not muzzle an ox while it threshes," and, "The worker is worthy of his wages."
verses.5:19: Do not entertain an accusation against an elder except on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
verses.5:20: As for those who persist in sin, reprove them in the presence of all, so that the rest also may have fear.
verses.5:21: I solemnly charge you in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus and of the elect angels to observe these things without prejudgment, doing nothing out of partiality.
verses.5:22: Do not lay hands hastily upon anyone, nor take part in the sins of others; keep yourself pure.
verses.5:23: No longer drink water exclusively, but take a little wine for the sake of your stomach and your frequent infirmities.
verses.5:24: The sins of some men are openly evident, going ahead of them to judgment, while the sins of others follow after;
verses.5:25: likewise good works also are openly evident, and even those that are otherwise cannot remain concealed.
verses.6:1: Let all who are bondservants under the yoke regard their own masters as worthy of full honor, so that the name of God and the teaching may not be blasphemed.
verses.6:2: And let those who have believing masters not despise them because they are brethren; rather, let them serve them all the more, because those who partake of the benefit are believers and beloved. Teach these things and exhort them.
verses.6:3: If anyone teaches a different doctrine and does not assent to sound words—those of our Lord Jesus Christ—and to the teaching that accords with godliness,
verses.6:4: he is puffed up with conceit and understands nothing, but has a morbid obsession with controversies and disputes over words, out of which arise envy, strife, slanders, evil suspicions,
verses.6:5: and constant friction among men who are corrupted in mind and bereft of the truth, supposing that godliness is a means of gain.
verses.6:6: Yet godliness with contentment is great gain indeed;
verses.6:7: for we brought nothing into the world, so that neither are we able to carry anything out;
verses.6:8: and having nourishment and covering, with these we shall be content.
verses.6:9: But those who desire to become rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many senseless and harmful desires that plunge men into ruin and destruction.
verses.6:10: For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil; reaching out after it, some have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
verses.6:11: But as for you, O man of God, flee from these things; rather, pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, steadfastness, and gentleness.
verses.6:12: Fight the noble fight of the faith; lay hold of the eternal life to which you were called, and you confessed the good confession in the presence of many witnesses.
verses.6:13: I charge you in the presence of God, who gives life to all things, and of Christ Jesus, who testified the good confession before Pontius Pilate,
verses.6:14: that you keep the commandment spotless and above reproach until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.6:15: which He will reveal in His own appointed times—He who is the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of those who reign and the Lord of those who rule,
verses.6:16: who alone possesses immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no man has seen nor can see; to Him be honor and eternal dominion. Amen.
verses.6:17: Charge those who are rich in the present age not to be haughty, nor to rest their hope on the uncertainty of wealth, but upon God, who richly furnishes us with all things for our enjoyment;
verses.6:18: to do good, to be rich in noble works, to be generous and willing to share,
verses.6:19: storing up for themselves a good foundation for the time to come, so that they may lay hold of that which is truly life.
verses.6:20: O Timothy, guard the deposit entrusted to you, turning away from profane, empty chatter and the opposing assertions of what is falsely called knowledge,
verses.6:21: by professing which, some have missed the mark regarding the faith. Grace be with you all.

notes.1:4: Greek oikonomian theou ("stewardship of God") refers to God's redemptive administration or plan; the em-dash marks an abrupt syntactic break (anacoluthon) in Paul's opening sentence.
notes.1:10: Greek arsenokoitais literally denotes "men who lie with men" (echoing the Septuagint of Leviticus 18:22 and 20:13), and andrapodistais refers to slave-traders or kidnappers.
notes.1:17: The Greek text reads mono theo ("the only God"); later Byzantine manuscripts add sopho ("the only wise God").
notes.2:7: The phrase en Christo ("in Christ") is present in the Greek source text, though omitted by several early manuscripts.
notes.2:12: Greek authentein ("to hold authority over") occurs only here in the New Testament and is variously understood as exercising governing authority or acting in a domineering manner.
notes.2:15: Greek dia tes teknogonias ("through childbearing") includes the definite article ("the childbearing"), leading interpreters to view it either as faithful perseverance in the calling of motherhood or as an allusion to the birth of the promised Seed (cf. Genesis 3:15).
notes.3:1: Greek episkopes ("the office of an overseer") is traditionally rendered "bishop" and is closely associated with the office of elder in the New Testament (cf. Titus 1:5-7).
notes.3:11: Greek gynaikas ("Women") can refer either to the wives of deacons or to women serving as deacons (deaconesses).
notes.3:16: The Greek text reads hos ("He who"), introducing an early Christological confession; later manuscripts read theos ("God"). Greek en pneumati may be understood as "in the Spirit" (the Holy Spirit) or "in spirit" in contrast with "in the flesh."
notes.4:10: Following the critical text, this verse reads "we strive" (Greek agonizometha) rather than the later textual variant "we suffer reproach."
notes.4:12: The critical Greek text lists five areas of example here, omitting the phrase "in spirit" found in later manuscripts.
notes.4:13: "The public reading" (Greek anagnosis) refers to the formal reading of the Scriptures in the gathered congregation.
notes.5:11: The rare Greek verb katastreniao denotes growing restive with sensual passions that draw one away from devotion to Christ.
notes.5:12: "Their first pledge" (literally "their first faith") likely refers to an earlier vow of dedicated service taken by enrolled widows.
notes.5:16: The critical Greek text specifies "any believing woman" (feminine piste), whereas later manuscripts expand this to "any believing man or woman."
notes.5:18: The first quotation cites Deuteronomy 25:4, and the second corresponds to the saying of Jesus recorded in Luke 10:7.
notes.6:2: "Those who partake of the benefit" is a debated Greek clause, most likely referring to the believing masters who benefit from their bondservants' faithful labor.
notes.6:5: The critical Greek text ends the verse here, omitting the closing clause "from such withdraw yourself" found in later manuscripts.
notes.6:7: The critical Greek text reads simply hoti ("so that") without the word "certain" (delon) added in later manuscripts to smooth the syntax.
notes.6:10: Because "root" (rhiza) lacks the definite article and precedes the verb, it is rendered "a root of all kinds of evil" (literally "a root of all evils").
notes.6:21: "You all" reflects the plural Greek pronoun hymon, indicating that the closing benediction extends beyond Timothy to the whole church; the critical text also omits "Amen."
